question: GQ-006
finding: Bifrost exposes a single flag that stops full body persistence; it is currently off.

the_flag.name: disable_content_logging
the_flag.effect: When true, Bifrost stops persisting request/response content — the 4.4 GB of raw_request and responses_input_history driving growth.
the_flag.scope: gateway-wide; token accounting, latency, cost and status are separate columns and are NOT content

contradiction_noted: config_log_store.config carries retention_days: 0 while config_client carries log_retention_days: 365. Two different fields; the client one is what the running gateway reports. Recorded rather than resolved — I did not want to assume which the daemon honours.
why_this_matters: Decision 6 was 'the log grows, what should we do'. It is now 'flip one boolean, keeping every number the routing evidence depends on'. Measured token/cost/latency columns survive; only the request and response bodies stop being stored.
not_applied: This is a gateway configuration change. Not a librarian decision (C-scope), and not applied.

token_survival_proof.note: Not an assumption. 176 rows in the live log already carry full token accounting with an empty raw_request, which demonstrates the columns are independent — disabling content logging cannot blind the routing or cache evidence.
